  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Knowledge as an act of the knower that corresponds to the known object; multiplicity of known objects entails multiplicity of knowledge acts unless the knowledge is identical with the essence itself.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal knowledge is direct apprehension; "second intention" (al-qaṣd al-thānī) is a metaphorical extension, rejected here as incoherent.
- Root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Multiplicity, abundance, increase in number.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In kalām, kathrah is opposed to divine unity (tawḥīd); any multiplicity in the divine essence is impossible.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal numerical plurality; used here to expose the contradiction in Avicenna's position.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Taqābūl (Contrastive Pairing) — When two terms are set in opposition (e.g., knowledge of self vs. knowledge of relation), the syntactic structure requires that each term retain its distinct referent, preventing conflation of meanings.
chapters.translation:
I say: The answer is from several angles. The first is that your statement — "He knows His essence as a principle" — is an arbitrary assertion. Rather, He ought to know only His own existence. As for the knowledge that He is a principle, this adds something beyond the knowledge of existence, because "principlehood" (al-mabdaʾiyyah) is a relation (iḍāfah) to the essence. It is possible to know the essence without knowing its relation, and were principlehood not a relation, then His essence would become multiple, and He would have both existence and principlehood — two distinct things. Just as a human being may know his own essence without knowing that he is an effect (maʿlūl) until he comes to know this — because his being an effect is a relation to his cause — so likewise, his being a cause is a relation to his effect. Thus the objection stands firmly against their mere claim that "He knows Himself as a principle," for in this there is knowledge of the essence and knowledge of principlehood, which is the relation, and the relation is other than the essence. Therefore, knowledge of the relation is other than knowledge of the essence, by the very proof we have mentioned: namely, that one can conceive of knowledge of the essence without knowledge of the principlehood, but one cannot conceive of knowledge of the essence without knowledge of the essence, because the essence is one. Since there are two known objects, there are two acts of knowledge.

The second angle is that their statement — "The whole is known to Him by a second intention" — is unintelligible speech. For whenever His knowledge encompasses something other than Himself, just as it encompasses His own essence, then He has two distinct known objects and two acts of knowledge regarding them. The multiplicity and distinctness of the known object necessitates multiplicity of knowledge, since one of the two known objects can be separated from the other in the imagination (al-wahm). Thus, knowledge of one is not identical to knowledge of the other; for if it were, it would be impossible to conceive of the existence of one without the other. And there is no "other" whenever the whole is one. This does not differ by expressing it as "second intention."

The universals are infinite! Then would that I knew how one dares to deny multiplicity while claiming that not an atom's weight escapes His knowledge in the heavens or on the earth, yet He knows the whole by a universal kind — and the universals known to Him are infinite. Thus, the knowledge attached to them, despite their multiplicity and distinctness, would be one in every respect.

Avicenna does not guard against the necessary consequence of "multiplicity." Indeed, Avicenna has opposed in this matter other philosophers who held that He knows only Himself, as a precaution against the necessary consequence of multiplicity. So how did he share with them in denying multiplicity, yet then diverge from them in affirming knowledge of the other? When he was ashamed to say that God knows nothing at all in this world or the next, but knows only Himself — while the other knows both himself and God, making the other more excellent than God in knowledge — he abandoned this out of shame for that doctrine and out of disdain for it. Yet he was not ashamed to persist in denying multiplicity from every aspect, claiming that His knowledge of Himself, of the other, and indeed of all things is His very essence without any addition. This is the very contradiction that the rest of the philosophers were ashamed of, due to its evident contradiction at first glance. Thus, no group of them is free from disgrace in their doctrine. And thus does God deal with one who strays from His path and imagines that divine matters can be mastered by his own speculation and imagination.

## $ Their claim that knowledge is by a single cognition, as in knowing the father and the son...

If it is said: "When it is established that He knows Himself as a principle by way of relation, then knowledge of the relative (al-muḍāf) is one. For whoever knows the son knows him by a single cognition, and in it there is knowledge of the father, of fatherhood, and of sonship implicitly. Thus the known objects multiply while the knowledge remains one. So likewise, He knows His essence as a principle for others, and the knowledge remains one even if the known objects multiply. Then, if this is understood in the case of a single effect and its relation to it, and it does not necessitate multiplicity, then an increase in what does not necessitate multiplicity by its kind does not necessitate multiplicity."

We say: Knowledge is by knowing the thing and by knowing the knowledge of the thing. Likewise, whoever knows a thing and knows his knowledge of the thing — he knows it by that knowledge. Thus, every knowledge is knowledge of itself and of its object, so the known objects multiply while the knowledge remains one.

You claim that God's known objects are infinite while His knowledge is one. This is also refuted by the fact that you yourselves hold that God's known objects are infinite and His knowledge is one, and you do not describe Him as having knowledges infinite in number. For if the multiplicity of the known object necessitated the multiplicity of the essence of knowledge, then let there be in God's essence knowledges infinite in number — and this is impossible.

chapters.title_en: Our Position Necessitates a Greater Multiplicity than Adding Existence to Essence
chapters.arabic_text:
### | قولنا يقتضي ذلك كثرة أكثر مما إذا أضيف وجود إلى ماهية

قلنا: مهما كان العلم واحدا من كل وجه لم يتصور تعلقه بمعلومين، بل يقتضي
ذلك كثرة ما على ما هو وضع الفلاسفة واصطلاحهم في تقدير الكثرة، حتى بالغوا
فقالوا: لو كان للأول ماهية موصوفة بالوجود لكان لذلك كثرة. فلم يعقلوا
شيئا واحدا له حقيقية ثم يوصف بالوجود، بل زعموا
أن الوجود مضاف إلى الحقيقة وهو غريه فيقتضي كثرة. فعلى هذا الوجه لا
يمكن تقدير علم يتعلق بمعلومات كثيرة إلا ويلزم فيه نوع كثرة أجلى وأبلغ من
اللازم في تقدير وجود مضاف إلى ماهية.
القول الأول باطل ... وأما العلم بالابن وكذى سائر المضافات ففيه كثرة،
إذ لا بد من العلم بذات الابن وذات الأب وهما علمان. وعلم ثالث وهو
الإضافة. نعم هذا الثالث  مضمن بالعلمين السابقين إذ هما من شرطه وضرورته
وإلا فما لم يعلم المضاف أولا لا تعلم الإضافة. فهي علوم متعددة بعضها
مشروطة في البعض. فكذلك إذا علم الأول ذاته مضافا إلى سائر الأجناس
والأنواع بكونه مبدأ لها افتقر إلى أن يعلم ذاته وآحاد الأجناس وأن يعلم
إضافة نفسه بالمبدئية إليها، وإلا لم يعقل كون الإضافة معلومة له.
... والثاني أيضا ... وأما قولهم: إن من علم شيئا علم كونه عالما بذلك
العلم بعينه فيكون المعلوم متعددا والعلم واحدا، فليس كذلك بل يعلم كونه
عالما بعلم آخر وينتهي إلى علم يغفل عنه ولا يعلمه. ولا نقول: يتسلسل إلى
غير نهاية، بل ينقطع على علم متعلق بمعلومه وهو غافل عن وجود العلم لا عن
وجود المعلوم، كالذي يعلم السواد وهو في حال علمه مستغرق النفس بمعلومه
الذي هو سواد وغافل عن علمه بالسواد وليس ملتفتا إليه، فإن التفت إليه
افتقر إلى علم آخر إلى أن ينقطع التفاته.
... وأما الثالث، فعليكم البرهان وأما قولهم: إن هذا ينقلب عليكم في
معلومات الله فإنها غير متناهية والعلم عندكم واحد، فنقول: نحن لم نخض في
هذا الكتاب خوض الممهدين بل خوض الهادمين المعترضين ولذلك سمينا الكتاب:
تهافت الفلاسفة، لا تمهيد الحق. فليس يلزمنا هذا الجواب.

### | قولهم في الأمر إشكال على جميع الفرق

فإن قيل: إنا لا نلزمكم مذهب فرقة معينة من الفرق. فأما ما ينقلب على
كافة الخلق وتستوي الأقدام في إشكاله فلا يجوز لكم إيراده، وهذا الإشكال
منقلب عليكم ولا محيص لأحد من الفرق عنه.

### | قولنا المقصود تشكيككم في دعاويكم

قلنا: لا، بل المقصود تعجيزكم عن دعواكم معرفة حقائق الأمور بالبراهين
القطعية وتشكيككم في دعاويكم.
أنتم تعترضون على المؤمنين بالرسول ... وإذا ظهر عجزكم ففي الناس من يذهب
إلى أن حقائق الأمور الإلهية لا تنال بنظر العقل، بل ليس في قوة البشر
الإطلاع عليه. ولذلك قال صاحب الشرع: تفكروا في خلق الله ولا تتفكروا في
ذات الله. فما إنكاركم على هذه الفرقة المعتقدة صدق الرسول بدليل المعجزة
المقتصرة  من قضية العقل على إثبات ذات المرسل المحترزة عن النظر في الصفات
بنظر العقل المتبعة صاحب الشرع فيما أتى به من صفات الله المقتفية أثره في
إطلاق العالم والمريد والقادر والحي المنتهية عن إطلاق ما لم يؤذن فيه
المعترفة بالعجز عن درك العقل.
... ونحن نعترض عليكم! وإنما إنكاركم عليهم بنسبتهم إلى الجهل بمسالك
البراهين ووجه ترتيب المقدمات على أشكال المقاييس ودعواكم أنا قد عرفنا ذلك
بمسالك عقلية. وقد بان عجزكم وتهافت مسالككم وافتضاحكم في دعوى معرفتكم وهو
المقصود من هذا البيان. فأين من يدعي أن براهين الإلهيات قاطعة كبراهين
الهندسيات؟

### | قولهم الأول لم يعلم إلا نفسه

فإن قيل: هذا الإشكال إنما لزم على ابن سينا حيث زعم أن الأول يعلم غيره.
فأما المحققون من الفلاسفة قد اتفقوا على أنه لا يعلم إلا نفسه، فيندفع هذا
الإشكال.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Knowledge, perception, and the act of grasping an object's reality; also the sign or trace by which something is known.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): ʿIlm as the apprehension of a thing's quiddity (māhiyyah) in its distinction from others; in divine discourse, it is an attribute entailing relation to the known.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) usage denotes direct apprehension; metaphorical (majāz) usage would be a loose extension—here, the philosophers' claim of a single knowledge encompassing many objects is scrutinized as a literal impossibility.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Exceptive Constructions (al-sharṭ wa al-istithnāʾ) — The text's "if... then..." (law... la-kāna) and "unless" (illā) structures govern the logical dependency of multiplicity upon relational knowledge, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say: Whenever knowledge is one in every respect, it is inconceivable that it should attach to two known objects. Rather, that would necessitate a multiplicity—precisely as is the very position and convention of the philosophers in estimating multiplicity. Indeed, they went so far as to say: If the First had an essence (māhiyyah) described by existence, there would be multiplicity in that. For they could not conceive of a single thing having a reality (ḥaqīqah) that is then described by existence; rather, they claimed that existence is added to the reality and is other than it, thus necessitating multiplicity. So on this very basis, one cannot posit a knowledge that attaches to many known objects without there necessarily arising in it a kind of multiplicity more evident and more forceful than what arises in positing an existence added to an essence.

The first claim is false... As for knowledge of the son, and likewise the rest of relational things (al-muḍāfāt), there is multiplicity in it—for one must have knowledge of the son's essence and the father's essence, and these are two knowledges. And a third knowledge, namely the relation (al-iḍāfah). Yes, this third is implicit in the two preceding knowledges, since they are its condition and necessity; otherwise, unless the related thing is known first, the relation is not known. So they are multiple knowledges, some of which are conditioned by others. Likewise, when the First knows His essence as related to all the genera and species by virtue of being their principle (mabdaʾ), He would need to know His essence, the individuals of the genera, and to know the relation of His essence to them through principality—otherwise, the relation's being known to Him is unintelligible.

... And the second [claim] also... As for their saying: "Whoever knows a thing knows, by that very same knowledge, that he knows it—so the known becomes multiple while the knowledge remains one"—this is not so. Rather, he knows that he knows by another knowledge, and it terminates at a knowledge that he is heedless of and does not know. And we do not say that this regresses infinitely; rather, it terminates at a knowledge attached to its known object while he is heedless of the existence of the knowledge—not of the existence of the known. Like one who knows blackness and, in the very state of his knowing, is wholly absorbed in his known object, which is blackness, heedless of his knowledge of blackness and not attending to it. For if he attended to it, he would need yet another knowledge, until his attention terminates.

... And as for the third [claim], the burden of proof is upon you. As for their saying: "This turns back upon you regarding God's knowledges, for they are infinite, and knowledge with you is one"—we say: We have not entered into this book with the entry of those who establish foundations, but with the entry of those who demolish and object. For this reason we have named the book: The Incoherence of the Philosophers (Tahāfut al-Falāsifah), not "The Establishment of Truth." So this answer is not incumbent upon us.

### | Their Saying: The Matter Poses a Difficulty Against All Sects

If it is said: "We do not hold you to the doctrine of any particular sect. But what turns back upon all creatures, and where all feet stand equally in its difficulty, you are not permitted to raise. And this difficulty turns back upon you, and no sect has any escape from it."

### | Our Saying: The Purpose Is to Cast Doubt Upon Your Claims

I say: No. Rather, the purpose is to incapacitate you regarding your claim to know the realities of things through apodictic demonstrations (barāhīn qaṭʿiyyah), and to cast doubt upon your claims.

You object to the believers in the Messenger... And when your incapacity has become manifest, there are among the people those who hold that the realities of divine matters cannot be attained by rational reflection; rather, it is not within human power to gain insight into them. For this reason, the master of the Law said: "Reflect upon the creation of God, and do not reflect upon the essence of God." So what is your objection to this sect—those who affirm the truthfulness of the Messenger by the evidence of the miracle, which confines the verdict of reason to affirming the existence of the One who sent him; who refrain from examining the attributes through rational reflection; who follow the master of the Law in what he has conveyed of God's attributes; who follow his trace in affirming that He is Knowing, Willing, Powerful, and Living; who refrain from affirming what they have not been permitted to affirm; and who acknowledge their incapacity for reason's attainment?

Rather, we object to you! Your objection to them is only by charging them with ignorance of the paths of demonstrations and the manner of arranging premises according to the figures of syllogisms, and by your claim that "we have known this through rational paths." Yet your incapacity has become manifest, your paths have shown their incoherence, and you stand exposed in your claim to knowledge—and this is the very purpose of this exposition. So where is the one who claims that the demonstrations of the divine sciences are apodictic like those of the geometrical sciences?

### | Their Saying: The First Knows Only Himself

If it is said: "This difficulty attaches only to Ibn Sīnā, who claimed that the First knows other than Himself. But the verifiers among the philosophers have agreed that He knows only Himself, and thus this difficulty is repelled."

chapters.title_en: Section 36 — On Their Claim That Every Rational Being Knows Many Things
chapters.arabic_text:
### | قولنا كل واحد من العقلاء يعلم أشياء كثيرة!

فنقول: ناهيكم خزيا بهذا المذهب، ولولا أنه في غاية الركاكة لما استنكف
المتأخرون عن نصرته. ونحن ننبه على وجه الخزي فيه، فإن فيه تفضيل معلولاته
عليه، إذ الملك والإنسان وكل واحد من العقلاء يعرف نفسه ومبدأه ويعرف غيره،
والأول لا يعرف إلا نفسه فهو ناقص بالإضافة إلى آحاد الناس فضلا عن
الملائكة، بل البهيمة مع شعورها بنفسها تعرف أمورا أخر سواها. ولا شك في أن
العلم شرف وان عدمه نقصان. فأين قولهم: إنه عاشق ومعشوق لأن له البهاء
الأكمل والجمال الأتم؟ وأي جمال لوجود بسيط لا ماهية له ولا حقيقة ولا خبر
له مما يجري في العالم ولا مما يلزم
ذاته ويصدر منه؟ وأي نقصان في عالم الله يزيد على هذا؟ بلغ الفلاسفة هذا
المبلغ! وليتعجب العاقل من طائفة يتعمقون في المعقولات بزعمهم ثم ينتهي آخر
نظرهم إلى أن رب الأرباب ومسبب الأسباب لا علم له أصلا بما يجري في العالم.
وأي فرق بينه وبين الميت إلا في علمه بنفسه؟ وأي كمال في علمه بنفسه مع
جهله بغيره؟ وهذا مذهب تغني صورته في الافتضاح عن الإطناب  والإيضاح.
الذات غير العلم بالذات، كما في الإنسان ثم يقال لهؤلاء: لم تتخلصوا عن
الكثرة مع اقتحام هذه المخازي أيضا، فإنا نقول: علمه بذاته عين ذاته أو غير
ذاته. فإن قلتم: إنه غيره، فقد جاءت الكثرة، وإن قلتم: إنه عينه، فما الفصل
بينكم وبين قائل: إن علم الإنسان بذاته عين ذاته؟ وهو حماقة إذ يعقل وجود
ذاته في حالة هو فيها غافل عن ذاته ثم تزول غفلته ويتنبه لذاته فيكون شعوره
بذاته غير ذاته لا محالة.

### | قولهم الإنسان قد يطرى عليه العلم فيكون غيره

فإن قلتم: إن الإنسان قد يخلوا عن العلم بذاته فيطرى عليه فيكون غيره لا
محالة.

### | قولنا يقدر طريان الذات

فنقول: الغيرية لا تعرف بالطريان والمقارنة فإن عين الشيء لا يجوز أن
يطرى على الشيء، وغير الشيء إذا قارن الشيء لم يصر هو هو ولم يخرج عن كونه
غيرا. فبأن كان الأول لم يزل عالما بذاته لا يدل على أن علمه بذاته عين
ذاته، ويتسع الوهم لتقدير الذات ثم طريان الشعور. ولو كان هو الذات بعينه
لما تصور هذا التوهم.
## $ قولهم ذاته عقل وعلم ...
فإن قيل: ذاته عقل وعلم فليس له ذات ثم علم قائم به.
## $ قولنا يردون الله إلى حقائق الأغراض! ...
قلنا: الحماقة ظاهرة في هذا الكلام، فإن العلم صفة وعرض يستدعي موصوفا،
وقول القائل: هو في ذاته عقل وعلم، كقوله: هو قدرة وإرادة وهو قائم بنفسه.
ولو قيل: به، فهو كقول القائل في سواد وبياض: إنه قائم بنفسه، وفي كمية
وتربيع وتثليث: إنه قائم بنفسه. وكذى في كل الأعراض. وبالطريق الذي يستحيل
أن تقوم صفات الأجسام بنفسها دون جسم هو غير الصفات،
بعين ذلك الطريق يعلم أن صفات الأحياء من العلم والحياة والقدرة والإرادة
أيضا لا تقوم بنفسها وإنما تقوم بذات. فالحياة تقوم بالذات فيكون حياته
بها، وكذلك سائر الصفات. فإذن لم يقنعوا بسلب الأول سائر الصفات ولا بسلبه
الحقيقة والماهية حتى سلبوه أيضا القيام بنفسه وردوه إلى حقائق الأعراض
والصفات التي لا قوام لها  بنفسها.
.. ولا يقيمون الدليل على كونه عالما ... وسنبين ذلك على أنا سنبين بعد
هذا عجزهم عن إقامة الدليل على كونه عالما بنفسه وبغيره في مسألة مفردة.

### | مسألة في إبطال قولهم أن الأول لا يجوز أن يشارك غيره في جنس

ويفارقه بفصل وأنه لا يتطرق إليه انقسام في حق العقل بالجنس والفصل

### | رأيهم

وقد اتفقوا على هذا وبنوا عليه أنه إذا لم يشارك غيره بمعنى جنسي لم
ينفصل عنه بمعنى فصلي، فلم يكن له حد إذ الحد ينتظم من الجنس والفصل، وما
لا تركيب فيه فلا حد له. وهذا نوع من التركيب. وزعموا أن قول القائل: أنه
يساوي المعلول الأول في كونه موجودا وجوهرا وعلة لغيره ويباينه بشيء آخر لا
محالة، فليس هذا مشاركة
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Disgrace, shame, ignominy; exposure to public reproach.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Moral deficiency entailing divine displeasure; used here as rhetorical indictment of philosophical doctrine.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of public humiliation; metaphorical extension to intellectual absurdity.
- Root: ر-ك-ك (r-k-k)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Thinness, flimsiness, weakness of texture; applied to argument as feebleness.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Deficiency in rational cogency; lack of demonstrative solidity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal physical thinness; metaphorical for logical fragility.
- Root: ب-ه-ج (b-h-j) / ج-م-ل (j-m-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Splendor, beauty, radiance; comeliness and perfection of form.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Divine attributes of majesty and beauty (al-bahāʾ wa-l-jamāl) as ontological perfections.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal aesthetic beauty; metaphorical for intellectual and existential nobility.
- Root: ع-ل-ق (ʿ-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Suspension, attachment, relation; that which hangs upon another.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Dependence of attributes upon a substrate (maḥall); ontological inherence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal hanging object; metaphorical for predicative dependence.
- Sībawayh Rule: Al-ʿAṭf ʿalā al-Ḍamīr al-Marfūʿ al-Muttaṣil (Coordination on the connected subject pronoun) — Permissible after separation by an intervening clause, as in "فإن فيه تفضيل معلولاته عليه" where the pronoun's referent is clarified by context.
chapters.translation:
I say: Sufficient for you is the disgrace of this doctrine! Were it not for its extreme feebleness, the later [philosophers] would have been too ashamed to champion it. We shall draw attention to the aspect of disgrace within it, for it entails preferring His effects over Him. For the angel, the human being, and every rational being knows himself, his principle, and knows others besides himself — whereas the First knows only Himself. Thus He is deficient in comparison to individual humans, let alone angels. Nay, even the beast, with its awareness of itself, knows other things besides itself. There is no doubt that knowledge is an honor and its absence is a deficiency. So where is their claim that He is lover and beloved because He possesses the most complete splendor and the most perfect beauty? And what beauty is there in a simple existence that has no quiddity, no reality, no information about what transpires in the world, nor about what necessarily attends His essence and issues from it? And what deficiency in the world of God exceeds this? The philosophers have reached such a depth! Let the rational man marvel at a group who delve deeply into intelligibles, as they claim, yet the end of their reflection is that the Lord of lords and the Causer of causes has no knowledge whatsoever of what transpires in the world. What difference remains between Him and the dead, except His knowledge of Himself? And what perfection is there in His knowledge of Himself, along with His ignorance of other things? This doctrine — its very form suffices for its disgrace without need for prolixity or clarification.

The essence is other than knowledge of the essence, as in the human case. Then one says to them: You have not escaped multiplicity even while plunging into these disgraces. For we say: His knowledge of His essence is either identical to His essence or other than His essence. If you say it is other than Him, then multiplicity has arisen. If you say it is identical to Him, then what distinguishes you from one who says that the human being's knowledge of himself is identical to himself? Yet that is folly, for one conceives the existence of his essence in a state wherein he is heedless of himself; then his heedlessness ceases and he becomes attentive to himself — so his awareness of himself is necessarily other than himself.

### | Their claim: Knowledge may supervene upon the human being, thus becoming other than him

If you say: The human being may be devoid of knowledge of himself, then it supervenes upon him and thus becomes other than him necessarily.

### | Our say: The supervention of the essence is conceivable

We say: Otherness is not known through supervention and conjunction. For the very identity of a thing cannot supervene upon that thing; and that which is other than a thing, when it is conjoined with the thing, does not become identical to it, nor does it cease to be other. The fact that the First has never ceased to know His essence does not indicate that His knowledge of His essence is identical to His essence. The imagination can extend to conceiving the essence, then the supervention of awareness upon it. Had it been the very essence, this conceivability would be impossible.

### | Their claim: His essence is intellect and knowledge

If it is said: His essence is intellect and knowledge — so He has no essence with knowledge subsisting in Him.

### | Our say: They reduce God to the realities of accidents!

We say: The folly is manifest in this statement. For knowledge is an attribute and an accident that requires a qualified subject. And one's saying, "He is in His essence intellect and knowledge," is like his saying, "He is power and will, subsisting by Himself." If it were said, "By Him," it would be like one saying of blackness and whiteness that they subsist by themselves, and of quantity, squaring, and cubing that they subsist by themselves. And likewise for all accidents. By the very path by which it is impossible for the attributes of bodies to subsist by themselves without a body that is other than the attributes — by that same path one knows that the attributes of living beings, namely knowledge, life, power, and will, also do not subsist by themselves but rather subsist in an essence. Life subsists in the essence, so its life is by it; and likewise for the rest of the attributes. Thus they were not content with divesting the First of all other attributes, nor with divesting Him of reality and quiddity, until they also divested Him of self-subsistence and reduced Him to the realities of accidents and attributes that have no subsistence by themselves.

... Nor do they establish proof of His being knowing... We shall show this — indeed, we shall show after this their incapacity to establish proof of His being knowing of Himself and of others, in a separate question.

### | Question on refuting their claim that the First cannot share a genus with another and differ from it by a differentia, and that no division by genus and differentia can apply to Him in rational consideration

### | Their view

They have agreed upon this and built upon it that if He does not share with another in a generic sense, He does not differ from it in a differentia sense. Thus He has no definition, since the definition is composed of genus and differentia; and that which has no composition has no definition. This is a type of composition. And they claimed that one's saying, "He equals the First Effect in being existent, substance, and cause of another, and differs from it by something else necessarily" — this is not a sharing...

chapters.title_en: On Genus (al-Jins) — That Existence Is Not a Genus Constituting Quiddity
chapters.arabic_text:
### | في الجنس

بل هو مشاركة في لازم عام.
في الجنس
وفرق بين الجنس واللازم في الحقيقة وإن لم يفترقا في العموم على ما عرف
في المنطق، فإن الجنس الذاتي هو العام المقول في جواب ما هو ويدخل في ماهية
الشيء المحدود ويكون مقوما لذاته. فكون الإنسان حيا داخل في ماهية الإنسان
أعني الحيوانية فكان جنسا. وكونه مولودا ومخلوقا لازم له لا يفارقه قط
ولكنه ليس داخلا في الماهية.
وإن كان لازما عاما، ويعرف ذلك في المنطق معرفة لا يتمارى فيها.
## $ قولهم إن الوجود لا يدخل في ماهية الأشياء ...
وزعموا أن الوجود لا يدخل قط في ماهية الأشياء بل هو مضاف إلى الماهية:
إما لازما لا يفارق كالسماء، أو واردا بعد أن لم يكن كالأشياء الحادثة،
فالمشاركة في الوجود ليس مشاركة في الجنس.
... ولا يدخل فيها "كونه علة" ... وأما مشاركته في كونه علة لغيره كسائر
العلل فهو مشاركة في إضافة لازمة لا تدخل أيضا في الماهية، فإن المبدئية
والوجود لا يقوم واحد منهما الذات بل يلزمان الذات بعد تقوم الذات بأجزاء
ماهيته. فليس المشاركة فيه إلا مشاركة في لازم عام يتبع الذات لزومه لا في
جنس. ولذلك لا تحد الأشياء إلا بالمقومات، فإن حدث باللوازم كان ذلك رسما
للتمييز لا لتصوير حقيقة الشيء. فلا يقال في حد المثلث إنه الذي تساوي
زواياه القائمتين، وإن كان ذلك لازما عاما لكل مثلث، بل يقال إنه شكل
يحيط به ثلاثة أضلاع.
... ولا يدخل فيها كونه جوهرا ... وكذلك المشاركة في كونه جوهرا، فإن
معنى كونه جوهرا أنه موجود لا في موضوع، والموجود ليس بجنس. فبأن يضاف إليه
أمر سلبي وهو أنه لا في موضوع فلا يصير جنسا مقوما، بل لو أضيف إليه إيجابه
وقيل موجود في موضوع لم يصر جنسا في العرض، وهذا لأن من عرف الجوهر بحده
الذي هو كالرسم له وهو أنه موجود لا في موضوع فليس يعرف كونه موجودا، فضلا
أن يعرف أنه في موضوع أو لا في موضوع، بل معنى قولنا في رسم الجوهر أنه
الموجود لا في موضوع أي أنه حقيقة ما إذا وجد وجد لا في موضوع. ولسنا نعني
به أنه موجود بالفعل حالة التحديد فليس المشاركة فيه مشاركة في جنس.
... بل الوجود الواجب هو للأول لا لغيره بل المشاركة في مقومات الماهية
هي المشاركة في الجنس المحوج إلى المباينة بعده بالفصل وليس للأول ماهية
سوى الوجود الواجب. فالوجود الواجب طبيعة حقيقية وماهية في نفسه هو له لا
لغيره. وإذا لم يكن وجوب الوجود إلا له لم يشارك غيره فلم ينفصل عنه بفصل
نوعي، فلم يكن له حد.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ج-ن-س (j-n-s)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Core meaning is "kind, sort, category"; in logic, the universal predicated in answer to "what is it?" (mā huwa), entering into the quiddity (māhiyyah) of the defined thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Genus (jins) is that which constitutes (muqawwim) the essence (dhāt), not a mere concomitant (lāzim); it is intrinsic to the thing's reality, whereas concomitants are extrinsic accidents of necessity.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage: genus as a real constituent of definition (ḥadd); metaphorical usage: any broad commonality, e.g., "participation in a general concomitant" — this is majāz, not ḥaqīqah.
- Root: ل-ز-م (l-z-m)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To adhere, cling, be inseparable; a necessary attendant (lāzim) that never parts from its subject.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A concomitant is that which follows the essence (dhāt) after its constitution, without entering into its quiddity; e.g., being created (makhlūqiyyah) for man.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: physical adhesion; metaphorical: logical inseparability — here used in the technical logical sense.
- Root: و-ج-د (w-j-d)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To find, to be; existence (wujūd) as the act of being found.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Existence is an accident (ʿaraḍ) added to quiddity (māhiyyah) — either necessary (as for the heavens) or contingent (as for originated things); it is not a genus because it does not answer "what is it?" but rather "that it is" (annahu).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal: being; metaphorical: the logical accident of existence predicated of quiddity — never a constitutive genus.
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Predication (al-Ḥaml) — The predicate (maḥmūl) in "what is it?" must be co-extensive with the subject's essence (dhāt) and constitutive of it; a mere concomitant, even if universal, cannot serve as a genus, just as a negative attribute (e.g., "not in a subject") cannot constitute a positive quiddity.
chapters.translation:
I say: Genus is but participation in a general concomitant. Yet there is a distinction between genus and concomitant in reality, even if they do not differ in universality, as is known in logic. For the essential genus (al-jins al-dhātī) is the universal predicated in answer to "what is it?" (mā huwa), entering into the quiddity of the defined thing and constituting its essence (muqawwim li-dhātihi). Thus, man's being alive — I mean animality (al-ḥayawāniyyah) — enters into man's quiddity and is therefore a genus. But his being born and created is a concomitant (lāzim) that never parts from him, yet it does not enter into the quiddity, even if it is a general concomitant. This is known in logic with a knowledge admitting no dispute.

## Their claim that existence does not enter into the quiddity of things...
They claimed that existence never enters into the quiddity of things; rather, it is added to the quiddity — either as an inseparable concomitant, as with the heavens, or as something arriving after not having been, as with originated things. Thus, participation in existence is not participation in a genus.

...Nor does "being a cause" enter into it... And as for His participation in being a cause for others, like other causes, it is participation in an added relational attribute (iḍāfah lāzimah) that likewise does not enter into the quiddity. For principality (al-mubdaʾiyyah) and existence — neither of them constitutes the essence (dhāt); rather, they adhere to the essence after the essence is constituted by the parts of its quiddity. So participation therein is only participation in a general concomitant whose adhesion follows the essence — not in a genus. For this reason, things are defined only by their constitutive elements (muqawwimāt); if one defined by concomitants, that would be a descriptive definition (rasm) for distinction, not for depicting the reality of the thing. Thus, one does not say in the definition of the triangle that it is "that whose angles equal two right angles," even though that is a general concomitant of every triangle; rather, one says it is "a figure enclosed by three sides."

...Nor does "being a substance" enter into it... Likewise, participation in His being a substance (jawhar). For the meaning of His being a substance is that He is an existent not in a subject (mawjūd lā fī mawḍūʿ), and "the existent" is not a genus. So if a negative attribute is added to it — namely, "not in a subject" — it does not become a constitutive genus. Even if one added its affirmation and said "an existent in a subject," it would not become a genus in the accidental sense. This is because one who knows substance by its definition, which is like a descriptive definition (rasm) of it — namely, "an existent not in a subject" — does not thereby know its being existent, let alone know whether it is in a subject or not in a subject. Rather, our saying in the descriptive definition of substance, "the existent not in a subject," means: a reality such that when it exists, it exists not in a subject. We do not mean by it that it is actually existent at the time of definition. So participation therein is not participation in a genus.

...Rather, necessary existence (al-wujūd al-wājib) belongs to the First alone, not to others. Participation in the constitutive elements of quiddity is what constitutes participation in genus, which then requires differentiation (mubāyanah) afterward by a differentia (faṣl). But the First has no quiddity other than necessary existence. Thus, necessary existence is a real nature (ṭabīʿah ḥaqīqiyyah) and a quiddity in itself, belonging to Him alone, not to another. And since necessity of existence (wujūb al-wujūd) belongs to none but Him, He does not share it with another, so He is not differentiated from anything by a specific differentia (faṣl nawʿī), and therefore He has no definition (ḥadd).

chapters.title_en: The Demand for Proof Against the Impossibility of Two Necessary Existents
chapters.arabic_text:
### | قولنا المطالبة

فهذا تفهيم مذهبهم. والكلام عليه من وجهين: مطالبة وإبطال. أما المطالبة
فهو أن يقال: هذا حكاية المذهب، فبم عرفتم استحالة ذلك في حق الأول حتى
بنيتم عليه نفي التثنية؟ إذ قلتم: إن الثاني ينبغي أن يشاركه في شيء
ويباينه في شيء والذي فيه ما يشارك به وما يباين به فهو مركب والمركب محال.
أبطلنا إمكان التركيب في الأول فنقول: هذا النوع من التركيب من أين عرفتم
استحالته؟ ولا دليل عليه
إلا قولكم المحكي عنكم في نفي الصفات وهو أن المركب من الجنس والفصل
مجتمع من أجزاء، فإن كان يصح لواحد من الأجزاء أو الجملة وجود دون  الآخر
فهو واجب الوجود دون ما عداه، وإن كان لا يصح للأجزاء وجود دون المجتمع ولا
للمجتمع وجود دون الأجزاء فالكل معلول محتاج. وقد تكلمنا عليه في الصفات
وبينا أن ذلك ليس بمحال في قطع تسلسل العلل، والبرهان لم يدل على قطع
التسلسل.
البرهان لا يدل إلا على قطع التسلسل فقط فأما العظائم التي اخترعوها في
لزوم اتصاف واجب الوجود به فلم يدل عليه دليل. فإن كان واجب الوجود ما
وصفوه به وهو أنه لا يكون فيه كثرة فلا يحتاج في قوامه إلى غيره، فلا دليل
إذن على إثبات واجب الوجود وإنما الدليل دل على قطع التسلسل فقط، وهذا قد
فرغنا منه في الصفات.
ليس بين الجنس والفصل مباينة تامة وهو في هذا النوع أظهر فإن انقسام
الشيء إلى الجنس والفصل ليس كانقسام الموصوف إلى ذات وصفة، فإن الصفة غير
الذات والذات غير الصفة والنوع ليس غير الجنس من كل وجه، فمهما ذكرنا النوع
فقد ذكرنا الجنس وزيادة. وإذا ذكرنا الإنسان فلم نذكر إلا الحيوان مع زيادة
نطق. فقول القائل: إن الإنسانية هل تستغني عن الحيوانية؟ كقوله: إن
الإنسانية هل تستغني عن نفسها إذا انضم إليها شيء آخر؟ فهذا أبعد عن الكثرة
من الصفة والموصوف.
إن لم تكن المباينة في الفصل ... ومن أي وجه يستحيل أن تنقطع سلسلة
المعلولات على علتين إحديهما علة السموات والأخرى علة العناصر أو أحدهما
علة العقول والآخر علة الأجسام كلها ويكون بينهما مباينة ومفارقة في المعنى
كما بين الحمرة والحرارة في محل واحد؟ فإنهما يتباينان بالمعنى من غير أن
نفرض في الحمرة تركيبا جنسيا وفصليا بحيث يقبل الانفصال، بل إن كان فيه
كثرة فهو نوع كثرة لا يقدح في وحدة الذات.
فمن أي وجه يستحيل هذا في العلل؟ وبهذا يتبين عجزهم عن نفي إلهين صانعين.
إما أن يكون هذا شرطا في وجوب الوجود وإما أن لا يكون، ولا يصح في
الحالين فإن قيل: إنما يستحيل هذا من حيث أن ما به من المباينة بين الذاتين
إن كان شرطا في وجوب الوجود فينبغي أن يوجد لكل واجب وجود فلا يتباينان،
وإن لم يكن هذا شرطا ولا الآخر شرطا فكل ما لا يشترط في وجوب الوجود فوجوده
مستغنى عنه ويتم وجوب الوجود بغيره.

### | قولنا يجب الكلام عن الموجود الذي لا علة له

قلنا: هذا عين ما ذكرتموه في الصفات وقد تكلمنا عليه. ومنشأ التلبيس في
جميع ذلك في لفظ واجب الوجود، فليطرح فإنا لا نسلم أن الدليل يدل على واجب
الوجود إن لم يكن المراد به موجود لا فاعل له قديم، وإن كان المراد هذا
فليترك لفظ واجب الوجود وليبين أن موجودا لا علة له ولا فاعل يستحيل فيه
التعدد والتباين ولا يقوم عليه دليل.
بعض التباين هو شرط في "كون" اللون لونا فيبقى قولهم: إن ذلك هل هو شرط
في أن لا يكون له علة؟ فهو هوس فإن ما لا علة له قد بينا أنه لا يعلل كونه
لا علة له حتى يطلب شرطه، أو هو كقول القائل: إن السوادية هل هي شرط في كون
اللون لونا؟ فإن كان شرطا فلم كان الحمرة لونا؟ فيقال: أما في حقيقته فلا
يشترط واحد منهما، أعني ثبوت حقيقة اللونية في العقل، وأما في وجوده فالشرط
أحدهما لا بعينه، أي لا يمكن جنس في الوجود إلا وله فصل.
فكذلك من يثبت علتين ويقطع التسلسل بهما فيقول: يتباينان بفصل، وأحد
الفصول شرط الوجود لا محالة ولكن لا على التعين.

### | قولهم وجوب الوجود كوجود اللونية لا كماهيته

فإن قيل: هذا يجوز في اللون فإن له وجودا مضافا إلى الماهية زائدا على
الماهية، ولا يجوز في واجب الوجود إذ ليس له إلا وجوب الوجود، وليس ثم
ماهية يضاف الوجود إليها. وكما أن فصل السواد وفصل الحمرة لا يشترط للونية
في كونها لونية إنما يشترط في وجودها الحاصل بعلة، فكذلك ينبغي أن لا يشترط
في الوجود الواجب فإن الوجود الواجب للأول كاللونية للون لا كالوجود المضاف
إلى اللونية.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ط-ل-ب (ṭ-l-b)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To seek, demand, or require; a claim or petition for evidence.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): A rational demand (muṭālabah) for demonstrative proof, distinct from mere assertion.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal sense of requesting; here, a technical dialectical move—pressing the opponent for a proof (burhān) of their premise.
- Root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Separation, distinction, or clarity; that which is manifest.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Mutual differentiation (mubāyanah) between essences, a key term in metaphysical discourse on plurality.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal separation; metaphorically, conceptual distinction without physical division.
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To cause, to be caused; a cause (ʿillah) or ground.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Causal relation (taʿlīl); the chain of causes (tasalsul al-ʿilal) central to the philosophers' proof.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal causation; here, the regress of causes and its termination.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional and Disjunctive Syntax (al-sharṭ wa al-taqsīm) — The text employs intricate conditional clauses (in kāna... fa-) and disjunctive reasoning (immā... wa-immā...) to structure the dialectical argument, requiring precise parsing of protasis and apodosis.
chapters.translation:
I say, in making the demand:

This is an elucidation of their doctrine. The discourse upon it proceeds from two angles: a demand for proof and a refutation. As for the demand, it is to say: This is a report of the doctrine—so by what means have you known the impossibility of that in respect of the First, such that you have built upon it the negation of duality? For you said: The second must share with Him in something and differ from Him in something; and that which has that by which it shares and that by which it differs is composite, and the composite is impossible. We have refuted the possibility of composition in the First, so we say: This type of composition—from where have you known its impossibility? There is no proof for it except your statement, reported from you in the negation of the attributes, namely that that which is composed of genus and differentia is assembled from parts. If it is possible for one of the parts, or for the whole, to have existence without the other, then it is the necessary existent without what remains; but if it is not possible for the parts to have existence without the composite, nor for the composite to have existence without the parts, then the whole is caused and dependent. We have already discoursed upon this in the section on the attributes and shown that this is not impossible in terminating the regress of causes, and the proof has not demonstrated the termination of the regress.

The proof demonstrates only the termination of the regress alone. As for the enormities they have invented regarding the necessary existent's being characterized by this—no proof has demonstrated it. For if the necessary existent is what they have described, namely that there is no multiplicity in it and it does not need another for its subsistence, then there is no proof for affirming the necessary existent; rather, the proof has demonstrated only the termination of the regress. This we have already completed in the section on the attributes.

There is no complete mutual differentiation between genus and differentia, and this is more evident in this type. For the division of a thing into genus and differentia is not like the division of the described into essence and attribute. For the attribute is other than the essence, and the essence is other than the attribute; but the species is not other than the genus in every respect. Whenever we mention the species, we have mentioned the genus plus an addition. When we mention "human," we have mentioned nothing but "animal" with the addition of "rational." So the statement of one who says: Does "humanity" dispense with "animality"?—is like his saying: Does "humanity" dispense with itself when something else is joined to it? This is further removed from multiplicity than the attribute and the described.

If there is no mutual differentiation in the differentia... And from what aspect is it impossible that the chain of caused things terminate in two causes—one being the cause of the heavens and the other the cause of the elements, or one being the cause of the intellects and the other the cause of all bodies—such that between them there is mutual differentiation and separation in meaning, just as between redness and heat in a single substrate? For they differ in meaning without our positing in redness a generic and specific composition such that it admits separation. Rather, if there is multiplicity in it, it is a type of multiplicity that does not impair the unity of the essence.

So from what aspect is this impossible in the causes? And by this their incapacity to negate two divine makers becomes evident.

Either this is a condition for necessary existence, or it is not; and it is not sound in either case. For if it is said: This is impossible only insofar as that by which there is mutual differentiation between the two essences—if it is a condition for necessary existence, then it should exist for every necessary existent, and so they would not differ. But if this is not a condition, nor is the other a condition, then everything not conditioned for necessary existence has its existence dispensed with, and necessary existence is completed by something other than it.

I say, it is incumbent to speak about that which has no cause:

We say: This is precisely what you have mentioned in the section on the attributes, and we have discoursed upon it. The source of obfuscation in all of this lies in the expression "necessary existent" (wājib al-wujūd). Let it be discarded, for we do not concede that the proof demonstrates a necessary existent, unless what is meant by it is an existent that has no agent and is eternal. If this is what is meant, then let the expression "necessary existent" be abandoned, and let it be shown that an existent having no cause and no agent—multiplicity and mutual differentiation are impossible for it—yet no proof stands for this.

Some differentiation is a condition for the "being" of color as color. So their statement remains: Is that a condition for its having no cause? This is nonsense. For that which has no cause—we have shown that its having no cause is not itself caused, such that its condition might be sought. Or it is like the statement of one who says: Is "blackness" a condition for color's being color? For if it were a condition, then why is redness color? It is said: As for its reality, neither of them is a condition—I mean the subsistence of the reality of colorness in the intellect. As for its existence, the condition is one of them, not specifically determined—that is, no genus can exist in existence except that it has a differentia.

Likewise, one who affirms two causes and terminates the regress by them says: They differ by a differentia, and one of the differentias is necessarily a condition of existence, but not specifically determined.

Their statement that necessary existence is like the existence of colorness, not like its quiddity:

If it is said: This is permissible in the case of color, for it has an existence added to the quiddity, additional to the quiddity; but it is not permissible in the case of the necessary existent, for it has nothing but the necessity of existence, and there is no quiddity to which existence is added. And just as the differentia of blackness and the differentia of redness are not conditions for colorness in its being colorness—they are only conditions for its existence attained through a cause—so likewise it should not be a condition in necessary existence. For the necessary existence of the First is like colorness for color, not like the existence added to colorness.

chapters.title_en: Section 39 — Refutation of Their Claim that the First's Existence is Simple, and the Demand for Proof
chapters.arabic_text:
### | قولنا كلا، وسيأتي الكلام عن الأمر

قلنا: لا نسلم، بل له حقيقة موصوفة بالوجود على ما سنبينه في المسألة
التي بعده. وقولهم: إنه وجود بلا ماهية، خارج عن المعقول. ورجع حاصل الكلام
إلى انهم بنوا نفي التثنية على نفي التركيب الجنسي والفصلي ثم بنوا ذاك على
نفي الماهية وراء الوجود، فمهما أبطلنا الأخير الوجود، فمهما أبطلنا الأخير
الذي هو أساس الأساس بطل عليهم الكل، وهو بنيان ضعيف الثبوت قريب من بيوت
العنكبوت.
العقلية مشتركة بين الأول والمعلول الأول المسلك الثاني الإلزام وهو أنا
نقول: إن لم يكن الوجود والجوهرية والمبدئية جنسا لأنه ليس مقولا في جواب
ما هو فالأول عندكم عقل مجرد، كما أن سائر العقول التي هي المبادئ للوجود
المسمى بالملائكة عندهم التي هي معلومات الأول عقول مجردة عن المواد، فهذه
الحقيقة تشمل الأول ومعلوله الأول فإن المعلول الأول أيضا بسيط لا تركيب في
ذاته إلا من حيث لوازمه وهما مشتركان في أن كل واحد عقل مجرد عن المادة
وهذه حقيقة جنسية. فليس العقلية المجردة للذات من اللوازم بل هي الماهية
وهذه الماهية مشتركة بين الأول وسائر العقول. فإن لم يباينها بشيء آخر فقد
عقلتم اثنينية من غير مباينة، وإن باينها فما به المباينة غير ما به
المشاركة
والعقلية.
وهذه المشاركة هي في ذات كليهما والمشاركة فيها مشاركة في الحقيقية فإن
الأول عقل نفسه وعقل غيره عند من يرى ذلك من حيث أنه في ذاته عقل مجرد عن
المادة، وكذى المعلول الأول وهو العقل الأول الذي أبدعه الله من غير واسطة
مشارك في هذا المعنى، والدليل عليه أن العقول التي هي معلولات أنواع مختلفة
وإنما اشتراكها في العقلية وافتراقها بفصول سوى ذلك، وكذلك الأول شارك
جميعها في العقلية فهم فيه بين نقض القاعدة أو المصير إلى أن العقلية ليست
مقومة للذات، وكلاهما محالان عندهم.

### | مسألة في إبطال قولهم إن وجود الأول بسيط

أي هو وجود محض ولا ماهية ولا حقيقة يضاف الوجود إليها بل الوجود الواجب
له كالماهية لغيره

### | المطالبة بالدليل

والكلام عليه من وجهين:  الأول المطالبة بالدليل فيقال: بم عرفتم ذلك؟
أبضرورة أو نظر؟ وليس بضروري فلا بد من ذكر طريق النظر.

### | قولهم يكون الوجود الواجب معلولا وهو محال

فإن قيل: لأنه لو كان له ماهية لكان الوجود مضافا إليها وتابعا لها
ولازما لها والتابع معلول فيكون الوجود الواجب معلولا وهو متناقض.

### | قولنا هو محال إذا لم يكن له علة فاعلية

فنقول: هذا رجوع إلى منبع التلبيس في إطلاق لفظ الوجود الواجب، فإنا
نقول: له حقيقة وماهية وتلك الحقيقة موجودة أي ليست معدومة منفية ووجودها
مضاف إليها، وإن أحبوا أن يسموه تابعا ولازما فلا مشاحة في الأسامي بعد أن
يعرف أنه لا فاعل للوجود بل لم يزل هذا الوجود قديما من غير علة فاعلية.
فإن عنوا بالتابع والمعلول أن له علة فاعلية فليس كذلك، وإن عنوا غيره فهو
مسلم ولا استحالة فيه إذ الدليل لم يدل إلا على قطع تسلسل العلل، وقطعه
بحقيقة موجودة وماهية ثابتة ممكن فليس يحتاج فيه إلى سلب الماهية.

### | قولهم تكون الماهية سببا فاعلا

فإن قيل: فتكون الماهية سببا للوجود الذي هو تابع له فيكون الوجود معلولا
ومفعولا.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: Existence and becoming; the copula of predication; that which is affirmed as a state (kawn) of a thing.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Existence (wujūd) as distinct from quiddity (māhiyyah); the ontological priority of existence over essence in necessary being.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage: existence as an attribute inhering in a subject; metaphorical: existence as identical to the subject (as philosophers claim).
- Sībawayh Rule: Rule of Predicate Complementation (al-ismād wa-l-takmilah) — The predicate (khabar) must complete the subject (mubtadaʾ) without circularity; here, the claim "existence is the quiddity" violates the syntactic-semantic need for a distinct predicate.
chapters.translation:
I say: We do not concede this. Rather, He has a reality (ḥaqīqah) described by existence, as we shall clarify in the question that follows. Their statement that He is "existence without quiddity" falls outside the intelligible. The sum of their discourse reduces to this: they built the negation of duality (tathniyah) upon the negation of generic and specific composition, then built that upon the negation of a quiddity beyond existence. So whenever we invalidate the last — which is the foundation of the foundation — the whole collapses upon them. It is a structure weak in establishment, akin to the houses of the spider.

The second path of obligation (ilzām) is this: We say — if existence, substantiality (jawhariyyah), and principality (mabdaʾiyyah) are not a genus, because they are not predicated in answer to "what is it?" (mā huwa) — then the First, according to you, is a pure intellect (ʿaql mujarrad), just as the other intellects which are the principles of existence — called "angels" by them, being the intelligibles of the First — are intellects abstracted from matter. This reality (ḥaqīqah) encompasses the First and His first effect (maʿlūluhu al-awwal), for the first effect is also simple, having no composition in its essence except in respect of its concomitants (lawāzim). Both share in that each one is an intellect abstracted from matter — and this is a generic reality. Thus abstract intellectuality (al-ʿaqliyyah al-mujarradah) is not among the concomitants of the essence; rather, it is the quiddity itself. And this quiddity is shared between the First and the rest of the intellects. If He is not distinguished from them by something else, then you have affirmed a duality without differentiation (mubāyanah). But if He is distinguished, then that by which differentiation occurs is other than that by which participation occurs — namely, intellectuality.

This participation is in the very essence of both; and participation in it is participation in the true reality (al-ḥaqīqah). For the First intellects His own self and intellects other than Himself — according to those who hold this view — inasmuch as He is in His essence an intellect abstracted from matter. Likewise, the first effect — which is the First Intellect that God originated without intermediary — shares in this meaning. The proof of this is that the intellects which are effects are of various species; their commonality lies only in intellectuality, and their differentiation lies in other differentiae (fuṣūl). So too, the First shares with all of them in intellectuality. Thus they are caught between breaking their own rule or conceding that intellectuality is not constitutive (muqawwimah) of the essence — and both alternatives are impossible according to them.

### A Question Concerning the Invalidation of Their Claim that the First's Existence is Simple

That is, He is pure existence (wujūd maḥḍ) with no quiddity and no reality to which existence is attributed; rather, necessary existence is to Him what quiddity is to other things.

### The Demand for Proof

The discourse against this proceeds from two angles. The first is the demand for proof. It is said: By what did you know this? By necessity (ḍarūrah) or by theoretical reflection (naẓar)? It is not necessary — so you must mention the path of reflection.

### Their Claim: Necessary Existence Would Then Be an Effect — Which Is Impossible

If they say: Because if He had a quiddity, existence would be attributed to it, dependent upon it, and necessary to it; and the dependent is an effect (maʿlūl) — so necessary existence would be an effect, which is contradictory.

### Our Reply: It Is Impossible Only If It Has an Efficient Cause

We say: This is a return to the source of obfuscation (talbīs) in their unrestricted use of the expression "necessary existence." For we say: He has a reality and a quiddity, and that reality is existent — that is, it is not non-existent or negated — and its existence is attributed to it. If they wish to call this "dependent" and "necessary to it," there is no quarrel over names (lā mushāḥḥah fī al-asmāʾ) once it is known that there is no agent (fāʿil) of this existence; rather, this existence has never ceased to be eternal (qadīm) without an efficient cause. If by "dependent" and "effect" they mean that it has an efficient cause — that is not so. But if they mean something else, that is conceded, and there is no impossibility in it. For the proof only establishes the cutting off of the chain of causes (qaṭʿ al-salāsil); and cutting it off by an existent reality and an established quiddity is possible — it does not require the negation of quiddity.

### Their Claim: The Quiddity Would Then Be an Efficient Cause

If they say: Then the quiddity would be a cause of the existence which is dependent upon it — so existence would be an effect and a product (mafʿūl).

chapters.title_en: Section 40 — On Their Claim That the First Is Not a Body, and the Futility of Their Proofs
chapters.arabic_text:
### | قولنا أي أنه لا يستغنى عنه

قلنا: الماهية في الأشياء الحادثة لا تكون سببا للوجود فكيف في القديم؟
إن عنوا بالسبب الفاعل له وإن عنوا به وجها آخر وهو أنه لا يستغنى
عنه فليكن كذلك فلا استحالة فيه، إنما الإستحالة في تسلسل العلل فإذا
انقطع فقد اندفعت الإستحالة، وما عدى ذلك لم تعرف استحالته فلا بد من برهان
على استحالته. وكل براهينهم تحكمات مبناها على أخذ لفظ واجب الوجود بمعنى
له لوازم وتسلم أن الدليل قد دل على واجب الوجود بالنعت الذي وصفوه وليس
كذلك كما سبق.
من الضلال أن يقال إن كل ماهية موجودة فمتكثرة وعلى الجملة دليلهم في هذا
يرجع إلى دليل نفي الصفات ونفي الإنقسام الجنسي والفصلي، إلا أنه أغمض
وأضعف لأن هذه الكثرة لا ترجع إلا إلى مجرد اللفظ وإلا فالعقل يتسع لتقدير
ماهية واحدة موجودة وهو يقولون:  كل ماهية موجودة فمتكثرة إذ فيه ماهية
ووجود. وهذا غاية الضلال فإن الموجود الواحد معقول بكل حال ولا موجود إلا
وله حقيقة ووجود الحقيقة لا ينفي الوحدة.
وجود بلا ماهية ولا حقيقة غير معقول المسلك الثاني هو أن نقول: وجود بلا
ماهية ولا حقيقة غير معقول، وكما لا نعقل عدما مرسلا إلا بالإضافة إلى
موجود يقدر عدمه فلا نعقل وجود مرسلا إلا بالإضافة إلى حقيقة معينة، لا
سيما إذا تبين ذاتا واحدة، فكيف يتعين واحدا متميزا عن غيره بالمعنى ولا
حقيقة له؟ فإن نفي الماهية نفي للحقيقة وإذا نفى حقيقة الموجود لم يعقل
الوجود، فكأنهم قالوا: وجود ولا موجود، وهو متناقض.
لا يعقل في المعلول نفي الماهية من الوجود ويدل عليه أنه لو كان هذا
معقولا لجاز أن يكون في المعلولات وجود لا حقيقة له يشارك الأول في كونه لا
حقيقة ولا ماهية له ويباينه في أن له علة، والأول لا علة له، فلم لا يتصور
هذا في المعلولات؟ وهل له سبب إلا أنه غير معقول في نفسه؟ وما لا يعقل في
نفسه فبأن ينفي علته لا يصير معقولا، وما يعقل فبأن يقدر له علة لا يخرج عن
كونه معقولا. والتناهي إلى هذا الحد غاية ظلماتهم فقد ظنوا أنهم
ينزهون فيما يقولون فانتهى كلامهم إلى النفي المجرد، فإن نفي الماهية نفي
للحقيقة ولا يبقى مع نفي الحقيقة إلا لفظ الوجود ولا مسمى له أصلا إذا لم
يضف إلى ماهية.

### | قولهم ماهيته هي أنه واجب

فإن قيل: حقيقته أنه واجب وهو الماهية.

### | قولنا الوجود غير المعلول لا يستغني عن الماهية

قلنا: ولا معنى للواجب إلا نفي العلة وهو سلب لا يتقوم به حقيقة ذات،
ونفي العلة عن الحقيقة لازم الحقيقة، فلتكن الحقيقة معقولة حتى توصف بأنه
لا علة لها ولا يتصور عدمها إذ لا معنى للوجوب إلا هذا. على أن الوجوب إن
زاد على الوجود فقد جاءت الكثرة، وإن لم يزد فكيف يكون هو الماهية والوجود
ليس بماهية؟ فكذى ما لا  يزيد عليه.

### | مسألة في تعجيزهم عن إقامة الدليل

على أن الأول ليس بجسم

### | قولنا وما الأمر إذا كان الأول جسما قديما؟

فنقول: هذا إنما يستقيم لمن يرى أن الجسم حادث من حيث أنه لا يخلوا عن
الحوادث، وكل حادث فيفتقر إلى محدث. فأما أنتم إذا عقلتم جسما قديما لا أول
لوجوده مع أنه لا يخلوا عن الحوادث فلم يمتنع أن يكون الأول جسما إما الشمس
وإما الفلك الأقصى وإما غيره؟

### | قولهم الأول لا يقبل القسمة والجسم لا يكون إلا مركبا

فإن قيل: لأن الجسم لا يكون إلا مركبا منقسما إلى جزئين بالكمية وإلى
الهيولى والصورة بالقسمة المعنوية وإلى أوصاف يختص بها لا محالة حتى يباين
سائر الأجسام، وإلا فالأجسام متساوية في أنها أجسام وواجب الوجود واحد لا
يقبل القسمة بهذه الوجوه.

### | قولنا أبطلنا هذا فيما سبق

قلنا: وقد أبطلنا هذا عليكم وبينا أنه لا دليل لكم عليه سوى أن المجتمع
إذا افتقر بعض أجزائه إلى البعض كان معلولا. وقد تكلمنا عليه وبينا أنه إذا
لم يبعد تقدير موجود لا موجد له لم يبعد تقدير مركب لا مركب له وتقدير
موجودات لا موجد لها، إذ نفي العدد والتثنية بنيتموه على نفي التركيب ونفي
التركيب على نفي الماهية سوى الوجود وما هو الأساس الأخير فقد استأصلناه
وبينا تحكمكم فيه.

### | قولهم الجسم بلا نفس لا يكون فاعلا

### | وإن كان له نفس فنفسه علة له

فإن قيل: الجسم إن لم يكن له نفس لا يكون فاعلا وإن كان له نفس فنفسه علة
له فلا يكون الجسم أولا.

### | قولنا كلا

قلنا: نفسنا ليس علة لوجود جسمنا ولا نفس الفلك بمجردها علة
لوجود جسمه عندكم بل هما يوجدان بعلة سواهما فإذا جاز وجودهما قديما جاز
أن لا يكون لهما علة.

### | قولهم كيف اتفق اجتماعهما؟

فإن قيل: كيف اتفق اجتماع النفس والجسم؟

### | قولنا وما المانع إذا كانا قديمين؟

قلنا: هو كقول القائل: كيف اتفق وجود الأول؟ فيقال: هذا سؤال عن حادث
فأما ما لم يزل موجودا فلا  يقال كيف اتفق. فكذلك الجسم ونفسه إذا لم يزل كل
واحد موجودا لم يبعد أن يكون صانعا؟

### | قولهم لأن الجسم لا يخلق غيره
chapters.anchors:
- Root: م-ه-ي (m-h-y)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: The core root denotes "that by which a thing is what it is" — the quiddity or essential constitution (māhiyyah) of an entity.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): In Kalām, māhiyyah is the intelligible essence distinct from existence (wujūd); its negation entails the negation of any real referent for existence.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal usage (ḥaqīqah) treats māhiyyah as the real essence; metaphorical extension (majāz) would empty it of content — Ghazali exposes the philosophers' slide into pure metaphor.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional apodosis with faʿ (فـ) — the protasis (sharṭ) introduced by "in" (if) is answered by a clause beginning with fa, marking the logical consequence; Ghazali deploys this to structure hypothetical refutations.
chapters.translation:
**Our Saying: That He Is Not Independent of It (the Essence)**

I say: The quiddity (māhiyyah) in originated things (al-ḥādithāt) is not a cause of existence — how then [could it be so] in the Eternal? If by "cause" they mean the efficient cause (al-fāʿil) of it, [we reject that]; and if they mean another aspect — namely, that He is not independent of it — then let it be so; there is no impossibility therein. Impossibility lies only in the infinite regress of causes (tasalsul al-ʿilal). When the chain is cut off, the impossibility is thereby removed. As for what is beyond that, its impossibility is not known — so a proof (burhān) of its impossibility is required. All their proofs are arbitrary judgments (taḥakkumāt) built upon taking the expression "necessary existence" (wājib al-wujūd) in a sense that entails certain concomitants (lawāzim), and assuming that the evidence has demonstrated necessary existence with the attribute they describe — but this is not so, as has preceded.

It is an error (ḍalāl) to say that every existing quiddity is multiplied [into essence and existence]. In sum, their proof in this matter reduces to their proof for negating the attributes (nafy al-ṣifāt) and negating division by genus and differentia — except that it is more obscure and weaker, because this multiplicity reduces to mere verbal expression. Otherwise, the intellect is capacious enough to conceive a single quiddity that exists — yet they say: "Every existing quiddity is multiplied, for in it there is quiddity and existence." This is the extreme of error, for the one existent is intelligible in every respect, and there is no existent save that it has a reality (ḥaqīqah); and the existence of the reality does not negate its unity.

**The Second Path: Existence Without Quiddity Is Unintelligible**

The second path is that we say: Existence without quiddity and without reality is unintelligible (ghayr maʿqūl). Just as we do not conceive pure non-existence (ʿadam mursal) except in relation to an existent whose non-existence is supposed, so we do not conceive pure existence (wujūd mursal) except in relation to a determinate reality — especially when a single essence (dhāt wāḥidah) is established. How then can one thing be determined, distinguished from others by meaning (maʿnā), yet have no reality? For negating the quiddity is negating the reality; and when the reality of the existent is negated, existence is not conceived. It is as if they said: "Existence with no existent" — which is self-contradictory.

It is not intelligible in the effect (maʿlūl) to negate quiddity from existence. Evidence of this: if this were intelligible, then it would be permissible that among effects there be an existence having no reality — sharing with the First in being without reality and quiddity, yet differing from Him in having a cause, while the First has no cause. Why then is this not conceivable among effects? Is there any reason for [its inconceivability] save that it is unintelligible in itself? What is unintelligible in itself does not become intelligible by negating its cause; and what is intelligible does not cease to be intelligible by supposing a cause for it. Their reaching this limit is the extreme of their darkness — for they fancied that they were exalting [God] in what they said, yet their discourse ended in bare negation (nafy mujarrad). For negating the quiddity is negating the reality; and with the negation of reality, nothing remains but the word "existence" with no referent (musammā) at all, unless it is attached to a quiddity.

**Their Saying: His Quiddity Is That He Is Necessary**

If it is said: "His reality is that He is necessary (wājib), and that is the quiddity" —

**Our Saying: Existence That Is Uncaused Does Not Dispense with Quiddity**

I say: There is no meaning for "necessary" except the negation of cause — which is a privation (salb) that cannot constitute the reality of an essence. The negation of cause from a reality is a concomitant (lāzim) of that reality. Let the reality be intelligible first, so that it may be described as having no cause and as not conceivable to be non-existent — for the meaning of necessity (wujūb) is nothing but this. Moreover, if necessity is additional to existence, then multiplicity has arisen; and if it is not additional, how can it be the quiddity, given that existence is not a quiddity? So it is like that which does not add to it.

**A Question: Disabling Them from Establishing the Proof**

That the First is not a body.

**Our Saying: What If the First Were an Ancient Body?**

I say: This [argument] only holds for one who holds that the body is originated (ḥādith) because it is not free from originated accidents (ḥawādith), and everything originated requires an originator (muḥdith). But as for you — if you conceive an ancient body (jism qadīm) with no beginning to its existence, while it is not free from originated accidents — why then is it impossible that the First be a body, whether the sun, or the outermost sphere (al-falak al-aqṣā), or something else?

**Their Saying: The First Does Not Admit Division, and a Body Is Only Composite**

If it is said: "Because a body is only composite (murakkab), divisible into two parts by quantity, into matter (hayūlā) and form (ṣūrah) by conceptual division, and into attributes peculiar to it necessarily, so that it is distinguished from other bodies — otherwise bodies would be equal in being bodies. And necessary existence is one, admitting no division in these respects" —

**Our Saying: We Have Already Refuted This**

I say: We have already refuted this against you and shown that you have no proof for it save that the composite, when some of its parts depend on others, is an effect (maʿlūl). We have discussed this and shown that if it is not improbable to suppose an existent with no existentiator (mūjid), then it is not improbable to suppose a composite with no composer (murakkib), and to suppose existents with no existentiator. For you have built the negation of number and duality upon the negation of composition, and the negation of composition upon the negation of quiddity other than existence — and that final foundation we have uprooted, showing your arbitrariness therein.

**Their Saying: A Body Without a Soul Cannot Be an Agent**

**And If It Has a Soul, Then Its Soul Is Its Cause**

If it is said: "A body, if it has no soul (nafs), cannot be an agent (fāʿil); and if it has a soul, then its soul is its cause — so the body cannot be the First" —

**Our Saying: Not So**

I say: Our soul is not the cause of the existence of our body; nor is the soul of the sphere, by itself, the cause of the existence of its body in your view. Rather, both are brought into existence by a cause other than themselves. So if their existence is possible as ancient (qadīm), then it is possible that they have no cause at all.

**Their Saying: How Did Their Conjunction Happen to Agree?**

If it is said: "How did the conjunction of soul and body happen to agree (ittafaq)?" —

**Our Saying: What Prevents It If Both Are Ancient?**

I say: This is like one who says: "How did the existence of the First happen to agree?" The answer is: This is a question about something originated (ḥādith). As for that which has never ceased to exist, one does not say "how did it happen to agree?" So likewise, the body and its soul — if each has never ceased to exist, why is it improbable that it be a maker (ṣāniʿ)?

**Their Saying: Because a Body Does Not Create Another**

chapters.title_en: The Soul Is Not Created Except Through the Body — and the Refutation of Their Proofs
chapters.arabic_text:
### | والنفس لا تخلق إلا بواسطة الجسم

فإن قيل: لأن الجسم من حيث أنه جسم لا يخلق غيره والنفس المتعلقة بالجسم
لا تفعل إلا بواسطة الجسم ولا يكون الجسم واسطة للنفس في خلق الأجسام ولا
في إبداع النفوس وأشياء لا تناسب الأجسام.

### | قولنا هذا أمر لا يدل عليه برهان

قلنا: ولم لا يجوز أن يكون في النفوس نفس تختص بخاصية تتهيأ بها لأن توجد
الأجسام وغير الأجسام منها؟ فاستحالة ذلك لا يعرف ضرورة ولا برهان يدل
عليه، إلا أنه لم نشاهد من هذه الأجسام المشاهدة وعدم المشاهدة لا يدل على
الاستحالة فقد أضافوا إلى الموجود الأول بما لا يضاف إلى موجود أصلا، ولم
نشاهد من غيره وعدم المشاهدة من غيره لا يدل على استحالته منه فكذى في نفس
الجسم والجسم.

### | قولهم الجسم يقدر بمقدار

فإن قيل: الجسم الأقصى أو الشمس أو ما قدر من الأجسام فهو متقدر بمقدار
يجوز أن يزيد عليه وينقص منه فيفتقر اختصاصه بذلك المقدار الجائز إلى مخصص
فلا يكون أولا.

### | قولنا وهذا المقدار يكون على حسب نظام الكل

قلنا: بم تنكرون على من يقول: إن ذلك الجسم يكون على مقدار يجب أن يكون
عليه لنظام الكل ولو كان أصغر منه أو أكبر لم يجز؟ كما أنكم قلتم: إن
المعلول الأول يفيض الجرم الأقصى منه متقدرا بمقدار وسائر المقادير بالنسبة
إلى ذات المعلول الأول متساوية ولكن تعين بعض
المقادير لكون النظام متعلقا به، فوجب المقدار الذي وقع ولم يجز خلافه،
فكذى إذا قدر غير معلول.

### | قولنا إذا أثبتم مبدأ للتخصيص

### | اضطررتم إلى تجويز التخصيص بغير علة

بل لو أثبتوا في المعلول الأول الذي هو علة الجرم الأقصى عندهم مبدأ
للتخصيص مثل إرادة مثلا لم ينقطع السؤال إذ يقال: ولم أراد هذا المقدار دون
غيره؟ كما ألزموه على المسلمين في إضافتهم الأشياء إلى الإرادة القديمة،
وقد  قلبنا عليهم ذلك في تعين جهة حركة السماء وفي تعين نقطتي القطبين.

### | فليطلق ذلك على غير المعلول أيضا

فإذا بان أنهم مضطرون إلى تجويز تميز الشيء عن مثله في الوقوع بعلة
فتجويزه بغير علة كتجويزه بعلة إذ لا فرق بين أن يتوجه السؤال في نفس الشيء
فيقال: لم اختص بهذا القدر؟ وبين أن يتوجه في العلة فيقال: ولم خصصه بهذا
القدر عن مثله؟ فإن أمكن دفع السؤال عن العلة بأن هذا المقدار ليس مثل غيره
إذ النظام مرتبط به دون غيره أمكن دفع السؤال عن نفس الشيء ولم يفتقر إلى
علة، وهذا لا مخرج عنه فإن هذا المقدار المعين الواقع إن كان مثل الذي لم
يقع فالسؤال متوجه أنه كيف ميز الشيء عن مثله، خصوصا على أصلهم وهم ينكرون
الإرادة المميزة، وإن لم يكن مثلا له فلا يثبت الجواز بل يقال: وقع كذلك
قديما كما وقعت العلة القديمة بزعمهم.

### | راجع ما سبق

وليستمد الناظر في هذا الكلام مما أوردناه لهم من توجيه السؤال في
الإرادة القديمة وقلبنا ذلك عليهم في نقطة القطب وجهة حركة الفلك.

### | الخاتمة

وتبين بهذا أن من لا يصدق بحدوث الأجسام فلا يقدر على إقامة دليل على أن
الأول ليس بجسم أصلا.

### | مسألة في تعجيزهم عن إقامة الدليل على أن للعالم صانعا وعلة

### | قولنا ما المانع أن يقال عن الجسم القديم أنه بغير علة؟

فنقول: من ذهب إلى أن كل جسم فهو حادث لأنه لا يخلوا عن الحوادث عقل
مذهبهم في قولهم: إنه يفتقر إلى صانع وعلة. وأما أنتم فما الذي يمنعكم من
مذهب الدهرية وهو أن العالم قديم؟ كذلك ولا علة له ولا صانع وإنما العلة
للحوادث وليس يحدث في العالم جسم ولا ينعدم جسم وإنما تحدث الصور والأعراض،
فإن الأجسام هي السموات وهي قديمة والعناصر الأربعة التي هي حشو فلك القمر
وأجسامها وموادها قديمة وإنما تتبدل عليها الصور بالامتزاجات والاستحالات
وتحدث النفوس الإنسانية والنباتية، وهذه الحوادث تنتهي عللها إلى الحركة
الدورية والحركة الدورية قديمة ومصدرها  نفس قديمة للفلك، فإذن لا علة
للعالم ولا صانع لأجسامه بل هو كما هو عليه لم يزل قديما كذلك بلا علة أعني
الأجسام. فما معنى قولهم إن هذه الأجسام وجودها بعلة وهي قديمة؟

### | قولهم لا يكون واجب الوجود وهو محال

فإن قيل: كل ما لا علة له فهو واجب الوجود وقد ذكرنا من صفات واجب الوجود
ما تبين به أن الجسم لا يكون واجب الوجود.

### | قولنا بل ينقطع تسلسل العلل

قلنا: وقد بينا فساد ما ادعيتموه من صفات واجب الوجود وأن البرهان لا يدل
إلا على قطع السلسلة، وقد انقطع عند الدهري في أول الأمر إذ يقول: لا علة
للأجسام وأما الصور والأعراض فبعضها علة للبعض إلى أن تنتهي إلى الحركة
الدورية وهي بعضها سبب للبعض، كما هو مذهب
الفلاسفة، وينقطع تسلسلها بها. ومن تأمل ما ذكرناه علم عجز كل من يعتقد
قدم الأجسام عن دعوى علة لها ولزمه الدهر والإلحاد كما صرح به فريق فهم
الذين وفوا بمقتضى نظر هؤلاء.
chapters.anchors:
- Root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To measure, proportion, and originate something upon a determinate measure; creation as bringing into being with precise estimation.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Origination (ījād) of a thing from nothing upon a determined measure; in Kalām, distinct from mere composition (tarkīb).
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal (ḥaqīqah) for divine creation; metaphorical (majāz) when attributed to creatures, implying causation by way of preparation (tahayyuʾ).
- Root: ع-ل-ل (ʿ-l-l)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: A cause (ʿillah) as that which necessitates an effect; recurrence of seeking the reason (taʿlīl).
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): The cause as that upon which the existence of another depends; in theology, the First Cause terminates the regress.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for causal necessity; metaphorical when used for mere occasion (sabab) in natural philosophy.
- Root: خ-ص-ص (kh-ṣ-ṣ)
  * Lisān / ʿAyn: To single out, distinguish, or specify (takhṣīṣ) a particular over its like.
  * Al-Rāghib (Mufradāt): Specification by a determiner (mukhassiṣ); central to the Kalām proof of the contingent world's need for a chooser.
  * Al-Zamakhsharī (Asās): Literal for setting apart; metaphorical for divine will (irādah) as the principle of particularization.
- Sībawayh Rule: Conditional apodosis with فاء (fāʾ al-jawāb) — the protasis (in qīla) is answered by a counter-conditional (qulnā) that reorients the burden of proof, following the pattern of argumentative exchange (muʿāraḍah).
chapters.translation:
I say: If it is said, "Because the body, insofar as it is a body, does not create another, and the soul attached to the body does not act except through the body — and the body cannot be a medium for the soul in creating bodies, nor in originating souls, nor in things that do not correspond to bodies" —

We say: Why is it not permissible that among souls there be a soul possessing a particular property (khāṣṣiyyah) by which it is prepared to bring forth bodies and non-bodies from itself? The impossibility of that is not known by necessity, nor does any demonstration indicate it — except that we have not observed it from these observed bodies. And the lack of observation does not indicate impossibility. For they have attributed to the First Existent what is not attributed to any existent at all, and we have not observed it from another; and the lack of observation from another does not indicate its impossibility from it. Likewise, then, regarding the soul and the body.

If it is said: The outermost body, or the sun, or whatever is measured among bodies — it is measured by a magnitude (miqdār) that admits of increase and decrease. Thus its being specified by that permissible magnitude requires a specifier (mukhassiṣ), so it cannot be first.

We say: What do you object to one who says: That body is upon a magnitude that it must be upon for the order of the whole (niẓām al-kull), and had it been smaller or larger, it would not have been permissible? Just as you yourselves said: From the First Effect (al-maʿlūl al-awwal) the outermost sphere emanates, measured by a magnitude, while all other magnitudes are equal relative to the essence of the First Effect — but the determination of some magnitudes is because the order is attached to it. Thus the magnitude that occurred was necessitated, and its contrary was not permissible. Likewise, then, when it is supposed as not an effect.

Rather, if they affirmed in the First Effect — which is, according to them, the cause of the outermost sphere — a principle of specification, such as will (irādah), the question would not cease, for it would be said: Why did He will this magnitude rather than another? — just as they imposed upon the Muslims for attributing things to the eternal will. And we have turned that back upon them regarding the determination of the direction of the heaven's motion and the determination of the two poles.

Since it is evident that they are compelled to allow the distinction of a thing from its like in occurrence by a cause, then allowing it without a cause is like allowing it with a cause. For there is no difference between the question being directed at the thing itself — "Why was it specified with this magnitude?" — and its being directed at the cause — "Why did it specify it with this magnitude over its like?" If the question about the cause can be repelled by saying, "This magnitude is not like another, for the order is tied to it and not to another," then the question about the thing itself can likewise be repelled, without needing a cause. There is no escape from this: for this determinate magnitude that occurred — if it is like the one that did not occur, then the question is directed: How was a thing distinguished from its like? Especially upon their principle, since they deny the distinguishing will. And if it is not like it, then permissibility is not established; rather, it is said: It occurred thus eternally, just as the eternal cause occurred, by their claim.

Let the examiner of this discourse draw upon what we have presented against them — the direction of the question regarding the eternal will, and our turning it back upon them regarding the pole-point and the direction of the sphere's motion.

And by this it is made clear that whoever does not affirm the origination (ḥudūth) of bodies is unable to establish any proof that the First is not a body at all.

A Question Concerning Incapacitating Them from Establishing a Proof That the World Has a Maker and a Cause.

We say: Whoever holds that every body is originated because it is not free of originated accidents — their doctrine is understood in their saying that it needs a maker and a cause. But as for you, what prevents you from adopting the doctrine of the Materialists (dahriyyah): that the world is eternal, likewise, with no cause and no maker? Rather, the cause is only for originated accidents. No body comes into being in the world, and no body perishes; only forms and accidents originate. For the bodies are the heavens, and they are eternal; and the four elements that fill the sphere of the moon — their bodies and their matters — are eternal. Only forms change upon them through mixtures and transformations. And human and vegetative souls originate. These originated things terminate in their causes to the circular motion, and the circular motion is eternal, and its source is an eternal soul of the sphere. Thus, there is no cause for the world and no maker for its bodies; rather, it is as it has always been, eternally so, without a cause — I mean, the bodies. So what is the meaning of their saying that these bodies have their existence through a cause, while they are eternal?

If it is said: Everything without a cause is necessary of existence (wājib al-wujūd), and we have mentioned of the attributes of the Necessary Existent what makes clear that a body cannot be necessary of existence —

We say: We have already shown the corruption of what you have claimed of the attributes of the Necessary Existent, and that demonstration indicates only the cutting off of the chain (qaṭʿ al-silsilah). And it is cut off at the very beginning for the Materialist, for he says: There is no cause for the bodies. As for forms and accidents, some are causes of others until they terminate in the circular motion — and some of its parts are causes of others, as is the doctrine of the philosophers — and their chain is cut off by it. Whoever reflects upon what we have mentioned knows the incapacity of everyone who believes in the eternity of bodies to claim a cause for them; and he is bound to materialism and heresy (ilḥād), as a group among them has explicitly declared — those who fulfilled the requirement of their own reflection.

chapters.title_en: Section 42 — On Their Claim that Bodies Are Not Necessary of Existence but Are Possible
chapters.arabic_text:
### | قولهم الأجسام غير واجبة الوجود فهي ممكنة

فإن قيل: الدليل عليه أن هذه الأجسام إما أن كانت واجبة الوجود وهو محال،
وإما أن كانت ممكنة وكل ممكن يفتقر إلى علة.

### | قولنا ولم لا تكون بغير علة؟

قلنا: لا يفهم لفظ واجب الوجود وممكن الوجود، فكل تلبيساتهم مغباة في
هاتين اللفظتين. فلنعدل إلى المفهوم وهو نفي العلة وإثباته، فكأنهم يقولون:
هذه الأجسام لها علة أم لا علة لها، فيقول الدهري: لا علة لها، فما
المستنكر؟ وإذا عني بالإمكان هذا فنقول: إنه واجب وليس بممكن. وقولهم:
الجسم لا يمكن أن يكون واجبا، تحكم لا أصل له.

### | قولهم إن الأجزاء تكون سابقة في الذات على الجملة

فإن قيل: لا ينكر أن الجسم له أجزاء وأن الجملة إنما تتقوم بالأجزاء وأن
الأجزاء تكون سابقة في الذات على الجملة.

### | قولنا لا يمكنكم الرد على إبطال الكثرة

قلنا: ليكن كذلك فالجملة تقومت بالأجزاء واجتماعها ولا علة للأجزاء ولا
